title: Making friends & social etiquette
intro:
Friendships in Japan often build slowly, through repeated contact in a shared setting: a hobby club ({サークル}), a sports team, a language exchange, volunteering, or regular colleagues. Showing up consistently matters more than one great conversation.

Invitations can be vague. {今度[こんど]、飲[の]みに行[い]きましょう} (let's go for a drink sometime) may be sincere or just friendly politeness. If you want to meet, follow up with a concrete day. Refusals are also indirect: {その日[ひ]はちょっと…} (that day is a bit...) is a clear no, and you shouldn't press for a reason.

Drinking parties ({飲[の]み会[かい]}) are a big part of social and work life. Wait for the toast ({乾杯[かんぱい]}) before drinking. It is polite to notice when someone's glass is empty and offer to pour. Many restaurants offer an all-you-can-drink course ({飲[の]み放題[ほうだい]}), and the bill is often split evenly ({割[わ]り勘[かん]}). You never have to drink alcohol; ordering oolong tea or a soft drink is completely normal.

Gifts are woven into daily life. After a trip, people bring souvenirs ({お土産[みやげ]}), usually individually wrapped snacks to share at work. When you visit someone's home, bring a small gift ({手土産[てみやげ]}), take your shoes off at the entrance, and say {お邪魔[じゃま]します}. If you receive a gift for a special occasion, a return gift ({お返[かえ]し}) is often expected.

With new acquaintances, start in polite speech and switch to casual speech when the other person does.

phrases.jp: 今度[こんど]、一緒[いっしょ]にご飯[はん]でもどうですか。
phrases.en: Would you like to get a meal together sometime?

phrases.jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の金曜日[きんようび]、空[あ]いていますか。
すみません、その日[ひ]はちょっと…。
phrases.en: Sorry, that day is a bit difficult...

phrases.jp: また誘[さそ]ってください。
お酒[さけ]はあまり飲[の]めないので、ウーロン茶[ちゃ]にします。
phrases.en: I can't drink much alcohol, so I'll have oolong tea.

phrases.jp: どうぞ、お注[つ]ぎします。
phrases.en: Here, let me pour for you.

phrases.jp: LINE、交換[こうかん]しませんか。
phrases.note: LINE is the dominant messaging app in Japan.

phrases.en: Excuse me for intruding. (entering someone's home)

phrases.jp: お邪魔[じゃま]しました。
phrases.en: Thank you for having me. (leaving someone's home)

phrases.jp: これ、旅行[りょこう]のお土産[みやげ]です。皆[みな]さんでどうぞ。
phrases.en: These are souvenirs from my trip. Please help yourselves, everyone.

phrases.jp: 素敵[すてき]なプレゼント、ありがとうございます。
phrases.en: Thank you for the lovely present.

phrases.jp: 今日[きょう]は誘[さそ]ってくれてありがとう。楽[たの]しかった！
phrases.en: Thanks for inviting me today. It was fun! (casual)

phrases.jp: 割[わ]り勘[かん]にしましょう。

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: マークさん、今週[こんしゅう]の土曜日[どようび]、何[なに]か予定[よてい]ある？
dialogue.en: Mark, do you have any plans this Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: 土曜日[どようび]？特[とく]にないよ。

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: 大学[だいがく]の友達[ともだち]とバーベキューするんだけど、一緒[いっしょ]にどう？
dialogue.en: I'm having a barbecue with some friends from university. Want to come?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いいの？ぜひ行[い]きたい！何[なに]か持[も]っていこうか。
dialogue.en: Really? I'd love to! Shall I bring something?

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、飲[の]み物[もの]をちょっとお願[ねが]いしてもいい？
dialogue.en: Then could you bring a few drinks?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: もちろん。何時[なんじ]にどこ？
dialogue.en: Of course. What time and where?

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: 11時[じゅういちじ]に駅[えき]の改札[かいさつ]で。費用[ひよう]は割[わ]り勘[かん]ね。
dialogue.en: At the station ticket gates at 11. We'll split the costs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: 了解[りょうかい]！楽[たの]しみにしてる。
dialogue.en: Got it! Looking forward to it.

tips: Follow up on vague invitations with a specific suggestion. If the other person keeps being busy, they may be politely declining.
At work drinking parties, juniors often pour for seniors. If someone pours for you, lift your glass slightly with both hands.
Bring small, individually wrapped souvenirs for your workplace after a holiday. It's a small effort that people notice.
In homes, also take off the house slippers before stepping on tatami, and use the separate toilet slippers if provided.
Switching to casual speech too early can feel pushy, and staying formal too long can feel distant. Mirror the other person.
